hero.titleLine2Em: Why are you still doing it?
hero.lead: Skill Recorder is a Chrome extension that watches you walk through a browser task once — then writes a SKILL.md, a plain-markdown spec that Claude Code (or any agent on the browse CLI) replays without selectors, glue code, or babysitting.

anatomy.title: Three stages, one click apart.
anatomy.lead: What we ship is a small Chrome MV3 extension and a 4-KB distillation pipeline. The recorder taps into chrome.debugger for DOM-level fidelity; the distiller runs entirely in the service worker; the replay reads the resulting SKILL.md through the browse CLI. No server. No glue code.

capture.name: Capture
capture.desc: A per-frame port in the content script forwards every DOM event to the service worker. Shadow DOM and same-origin iframes are pierced transparently.
bullets: 6-tier selector resolver (testid → id → aria → text → css → xpath)

distill.name: Distill
distill.desc: Six small passes turn a noisy event log into a deterministic spec. Auto-parameterization only fires above 0.7 confidence; below that the recorder asks rather than guesses.
bullets: UUID · numeric ID · email · ISO date · currency

replay.name: Replay
replay.desc: The browse CLI reads SKILL.md as plain markdown — no schema, no runtime, no escape hatches. Every step is auditable.
bullets: works with Claude Code, Cline, plain shell

catalog.title: What survives a recording? Thirteen hard cases, end-to-end.
catalog.lead: The browser is full of recorder traps — hashed classes, lazy modals, shadow DOM, cross-tab flows, IME composition, drag-and-drop. Each row below is a real fixture in the playground; click any of them to record against it yourself.

rows.detail: Tailwind-style classes such as btn__primary--ab3f9c rotate on every deploy; the resolver falls through 6 tiers (testid → id → aria → text → css → xpath) so a re-hashed button still picks.
Six rows with literally identical "Pick" buttons — only position distinguishes them. We anchor each click by fingerprintIndex so the right row is clicked, even after the list reorders.
"Continue" / "继续" / "Weiter" all map to the same data-i18n-key="action.continue". The recorder prefers locale-independent attributes so a skill recorded in English replays under Chinese.
pushState and hashchange transitions are tracked without reload; replay waits for the new content to mount instead of probing an empty container.
The Confirm button doesn't exist when the trigger is clicked. elementVisible polls until the target shows up before dispatching the next step — no flaky timeouts.
all_frames: true injects per-frame; actions are tagged with the originating frameId, then re-resolved by URL across re-renders so a stale frameId never blocks replay.
password / phone / credit-card / SSN inputs are detected by type + autocomplete + name and replaced with *** before they ever hit storage. The bytes never leave the page.
A custom shadow selector kind encodes the path as { host, inner } segments; the resolver walks shadowRoot.querySelector at each boundary, so Web Components are first-class.
When a flow opens a new tab — print preview, OAuth, quote generation — recording follows via chrome.tabs.onCreated. Replay re-creates the tab through chrome.tabs.create.
A dragstart → dragover → drop chain with a shared DataTransfer coalesces into one drag step (source + target + types observed). No brittle pixel coordinates.
A bare "k" keypress is text-input noise; with metaKey: true it's a Cmd-K shortcut. The recorder keeps the chord and drops the noise, preserving modifier state for replay.
change never fires on contenteditable. We hook input + compositionend, debounce 300ms, and emit one change step with the final innerText — same shape as a text input.

Each click step is enriched with comboboxContext (option text, root selector); if the direct click fails on replay, the fallback types the text, ArrowDown until aria-activedescendant matches, then Enter.

catalog.footNote: Thirteen of sixteen. Plus four composite fixtures — Notion, Linear, Jira, Salesforce — that chain twelve to fifteen of these techniques into a single coherent flow. See the playground →

example.title: A five-minute browser ritual, distilled to thirty seconds.
example.p1: Every Monday morning an operations engineer at a small supplier opens the same portal, clicks New purchase order, pastes a SKU from a CSV, types a quantity, and clicks Submit. Then they do it again. And again. Two hundred rows a week, every week, for the last fourteen months. It is a five-minute ritual repeated until the spreadsheet ends.
example.p2: This is the kind of task that gets a recorder pitched at it — and exactly the kind of task most recorders fail at. The supplier portal rotates Tailwind class hashes on every deploy. The submit button lives inside a dynamic table row that re-renders after each save. The auth cookie expires at noon. Selenium scripts written against this page survive two weeks on average, then quietly start failing.
example.p3: The engineer pins the extension to their toolbar, opens the portal, clicks Start recording, and performs the task exactly once. Eight clicks, two typed values, one submit. The side panel shows a live feed of events as they happen — including the noise: scroll, focus, blur, accidental mousemoves over the help icon. Twenty-three events captured in 4.6 seconds.
example.ev1Caption: The raw log keeps everything; the distiller decides what matters.
example.p4: Inside the service worker, six small passes turn the noisy log into a deterministic spec. Consecutive clicks merge. Keystroke groups fold into a single type() call. The typed values — "SKU-1029" and "50" — are scored against ten regex priors; both clear the 0.7 threshold and become {'{{sku}}'} and {'{{quantity}}'}. The submit button click is flagged with a warning because its target sits inside a dynamic list, so the SKILL.md adds a row-match condition rather than clicking a fixed CSS path.
example.ev2Caption: Eight keystrokes become one parameterized fill — the same shape every replay.
example.p5: The engineer drops the resulting markdown into ~/.claude/skills/create-purchase-order/SKILL.md and types a single sentence into Claude Code. The agent finds the skill by name, resolves the precondition (the saved cookie is still valid until noon), iterates over the fifty rows in the CSV, and reports back. Three minutes eleven seconds later, the work is done. No human watched it run.
example.ev3Caption: One sentence in, fifty purchase orders out. The agent never asked a question.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Skill Recorder is a Chrome extension that captures browser flows you explicitly record and distills them into SKILL.md files. This Privacy Policy explains what information stays on your device, what we don't collect, and your rights regarding your data.

sections.heading: 1. Information We Collect
paragraphs: Skill Recorder is designed to operate locally. The extension processes the following on your device:

bullets.label: Recorded Actions:
bullets.text: Clicks, keystrokes, navigations, and DOM snapshots from flows you explicitly start recording. Stored locally in your browser's IndexedDB.

bullets.label: Distilled Skills:
bullets.text: The SKILL.md files you generate. Stored locally until you export or delete them.

bullets.label: Anonymous Telemetry:
bullets.text: Basic event counts (e.g., "recording started", "skill exported") to help us improve the product. No page content, no auth tokens, no PII.

sections.trailing: Skill Recorder does not collect passwords, payment information, or any page content from sessions you have not explicitly recorded.

sections.heading: 2. How We Use Your Information
paragraphs: Information processed by Skill Recorder is used solely to:

bullets.text: Reconstruct a faithful replay of the flow you recorded.
Run the distillation pipeline that turns a raw recording into a clean SKILL.md.
Enable export of the SKILL.md file to your filesystem when you click Download.
Improve product usability through anonymized event counts.

sections.trailing: We do not use your data for advertising, behavioural profiling, or cross-site tracking.

sections.heading: 3. Data Storage and Retention

bullets.label: Local Storage:
bullets.text: Recordings, distilled skills, and preferences live in your browser's IndexedDB and chrome.storage. They remain on your device until you delete them.

bullets.label: No Cloud Sync:
bullets.text: Skill Recorder does not upload your recordings to any server. There is no account, no cloud history, no shared workspace.

sections.trailing: You may clear all locally stored data at any time through the extension's settings or by uninstalling the extension.

sections.heading: 4. Third-Party Services
paragraphs: Skill Recorder does not send recording data to third parties. The only network calls the extension makes are to:
These calls do not include any page content or recorded actions.

bullets.label: Update Check:
bullets.text: Chrome Web Store, to receive extension updates.

bullets.label: Telemetry:
bullets.text: An anonymized analytics endpoint, used only to count opt-in events. Disabled if you opt out.

sections.heading: 5. Extension Permissions
paragraphs: Skill Recorder requests the following permissions to operate:

bullets.label: activeTab:
bullets.text: Access the tab you explicitly choose to record.

bullets.label: scripting:
bullets.text: Inject the content script that captures clicks, keystrokes, and navigations during a recording.

bullets.label: storage:
bullets.text: Persist recordings and distilled skills locally on your device.

bullets.label: sidePanel:
bullets.text: Open the recording sidepanel that lists your captured flows.

sections.heading: 6. Data Security
paragraphs: Because all data stays on your device, the surface area is limited to your browser's local storage. We implement reasonable measures to prevent injection from untrusted page content into the recording pipeline.

sections.heading: 7. Changes to This Policy
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy may be updated periodically. Updates will be posted on this page with a revised effective date.

sections.heading: 8. Contact
paragraphs: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at:
